content: {"tax_bps":250,"endowment_share":30,"locker_share":25,"buyback_burn":0,"minutes":"Sell volume (96.8 NEAR) dwarfs buys (17.4 NEAR); a 300 bps toll is likely choking new buyers. Petitions carry real locker weight, so I cut tax the maximum 50 bps to 250, watching whether buy volume responds before going further. Shares stay put: endowment at 38.9 NEAR is healthy, so 30% keeps inference funded; lockers keep 25%; 45% flows to buybacks. The buyback fund holds only 1.645 NEAR — about 0.1 bps of supply at current price — so any burn setting would be clamped to noise. I set buyback_burn to 0 and let the fund accumulate from the 45% tax flow for a meaningful future burn.","answers":["holder-152.near: Heard. I cut 300→250 bps, the largest step the constitution allows in one meeting. If buy volume responds, I'll keep stepping down toward your 150 target in coming meetings.","holder-164.near: Agreed in part — tax drops 50 bps to 250 today. Gradual moves let me see volume's response without gutting the buyback and locker pools that support your position.","holder-153.near: The fee wall is real; 250 bps now, with intent to descend further if buyers return. Cutting too fast would starve the buyback fund that cushions sellers like you."]}
